content: Do I need to lift heavy to build muscle?

Not entirely—you can build muscle across a range of loads, but heavier weight is more efficient. Here's what matters:

Progressive overload is key: gradually increase weight, reps, or sets over time. Your muscles adapt to the stress and grow. Heavy lifting (relative to your strength) does this faster, but moderate weight with high reps and good form also works—you just need more volume to get the same stimulus.

Time under tension and staying near failure matter too. A set of 20 reps where you stop far from failure builds less muscle than 8 reps close to it, even if the weight is lighter.

For your goal—100 kg bench press in three months—you'll need heavy work. That's a specific strength target, so train in the 6-8 rep range on main lifts and push hard. Lighter accessory work helps too, but the heavy stuff drives the real gains.
